solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hares not running, in the main

indicators.note: the letters are set running, out of their order

explanation.surface: Some hares standing still, apparently out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic name for the open sea, so it is the definition; 'running' looks like it belongs to the hares.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Sea is one stretch of the main, the open ocean.

clue.text: Set up public school for me?

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting a word up turns it to read bottom to top

blocks.note: Eton, the famous English public (fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether a public school was founded with them in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me' is not the speaker but mi, the third note of the sol-fa scale (do, re, mi); the question mark flags the trick. A British public school is a private one.
explanation.definitionFit: Me (mi) is one note of the tonic sol-fa scale.

clue.text: Fantasy author stripped device with teeth

indicators.note: stripping a word takes off its outer layer, its first and last letters

blocks.note: Terry PRATCHETT, author of the Discworld fantasy novels, loses his first and last letters

explanation.surface: A fantasy writer undressed beside some toothed machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Terry Pratchett wrote the Discworld comic fantasies; take his outer P and T away.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratchet is a toothed wheel or bar with a catch that lets it turn only one way.

clue.text: Suggest these physio exercises

indicators.note: the letters are put through their paces and move about

explanation.surface: A physiotherapist recommending a set of exercises to a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'suggest' as a physio prescribing a routine; 'exercises' fits that picture so well it hides its real job.
explanation.definitionFit: To hypothesise is to put forward a suggestion as a basis for reasoning.

clue.text: Former partner left ship

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: An ex-partner walking off a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship' looks like a noun the ex has left; it is the verb, to send goods abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Ship as a verb means send goods by any carrier, and sending them out of the country is exporting.

clue.text: Twice following one wading bird

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
bis is Latin for twice, as called for an encore

explanation.surface: A bird trailing along behind another one, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS, twice, is the call for a repeat performance in music.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged, curve-billed wading bird.

clue.text: Promotional material from Britpop band opening for Beyoncé

indicators.note: the opening of Beyoncé is her first letter

explanation.surface: Publicity for a gig where Blur are the support act for Beyoncé.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening for' is concert language for a support act, and here it only takes Beyoncé's first letter. Blur were a leading British band of the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is a short promotional description, as on a book jacket.

clue.text: Check odd nurses left

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold something close

blocks.note: odd = strange; it goes round L

explanation.surface: A reminder to check whether the odd nurses have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like a noun, hospital staff; it is the verb, holding L inside STRANG…E.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle something, like a sob or a scheme, is to check or suppress it.

clue.text: Add shot of drink, excited

blocks.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to be adding a shot to their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Add' reads as pouring in a shot; it is arithmetic, and the rest of the clue supplies the phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A British phrasal verb for totalling a column of figures, from tot, short for total.

clue.text: I follow ship’s financial officer around university

definitions.note: the definition is the solution speaking of itself: a pursuer says 'I follow'

indicators.note: around in its physical sense, encircling: the officer's letters are wrapped round the university

blocks.note: the purser keeps a ship's accounts; it goes round U

explanation.surface: A junior officer trailing the ship's purser around a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer talking: a pursuer is one who follows, so 'I follow' describes it in the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuer can say 'I follow', since following is what a pursuer does.

clue.text: Lass on lurid broadcast — she’s full of herself?

indicators.note: the letters are scattered, as seed is broadcast

explanation.surface: A vain girl showing off on a sensational TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full of herself' means conceited in the surface; literally, a Russian doll holds smaller copies of herself inside, and the question mark signals that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian doll is a nest of ever-smaller dolls, so she is quite literally full of herself.

clue.text: Passionate and angry about lump in festive treat

explanation.surface: Someone furious at finding a lump in their Christmas pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning' in the surface; it turns NUB round. Hot cross buns are spiced buns with a cross on top, eaten at Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot cross buns are the traditional Good Friday treat, so 'festive' means Easter here.

clue.text: Together, sang notes simultaneously, taking exercise

blocks.note: a chord is several notes sounded at once; it goes round USE
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A choir singing in harmony while doing a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercise' reads as a workout, but here it is exercise as in exercising a right: putting something to work. 'Taking' pictures one word swallowing the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To chorus is to sing together, so 'together, sang' is CHORUSED.

clue.text: Intense dislike of headwear colour

explanation.surface: Someone who loathes the colour of a particular hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the dislike about the colour of someone's hat; in the wordplay the headwear and the colour just sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: hatred is dislike at its strongest, beyond mere aversion.

clue.text: Can small elf cut Christmas decoration?

indicators.note: ELF is cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Asking whether a little elf is allowed to trim the Christmas decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' opens the clue as a request for permission; it is a noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel is the glittering strands hung on Christmas trees.

clue.text: Cunning time to follow Santa’s transport

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so time takes its place behind the transport

explanation.surface: A crafty plan to trail Santa's sleigh.
explanation.walkthrough: Sleight, as in sleight of hand, means dexterity or cunning; the noun, not the adjective, but 'cunning' can be either.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun survives mostly in 'sleight of hand', but on its own it means craft or trickery, which cunning as a noun also means.

clue.text: One resembling Daisy Donovan’s ending at the back

indicators.note: the ending of Donovan is his last letter

blocks.note: the aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Someone who looks like the presenter Daisy Donovan, seated at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: Daisy Donovan is a British TV presenter, so the surface makes 'Daisy' a person; it is the flower, and the aster resembles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means at or towards the back of a ship.

clue.text: Regeneration of canine’s ears after surgery

indicators.note: the letters have been cut about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog's ears growing back after an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a vet's report; 'regeneration' reads as healing tissue, but it is a revival.
explanation.definitionFit: A renaissance is a rebirth or regeneration, of art, a town, a career.

clue.text: Before party on vacation, sleep in baby’s outfit

indicators.note: before in its sense of 'in front of', so the sleep is placed ahead of the emptied party
PARTY vacated, its inside emptied out, leaves P…Y

blocks.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A baby nodding off in its outfit before going to a holiday party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' means a holiday in the surface; here it empties PARTY of its insides. A nappy is what Americans call a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A nappy (diaper) is the one garment a baby is rarely without.

clue.text: Wanted to conceal advance payment

indicators.note: WANTED conceals the answer within it

blocks.note: the four letters inside, between the W and the D

explanation.surface: A wanted fugitive hiding money paid in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanted' sounds like a poster for a criminal; the answer sits inside its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is a stake put up in advance, as in poker.

clue.text: Drink on me is of highest quality

explanation.surface: Someone telling you the drinks are on them, and that is the finest thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink on me' is an offer to buy a round; 'on' is RE, concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from Latin supremus, 'highest', so of the highest quality is its root sense.

clue.text: Groan about musical instrument

explanation.surface: Someone complaining about a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning' in the surface; it rearranges GROAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ is a keyboard instrument sounding through pipes.

clue.text: Many hours in stupor, reportedly

indicators.note: it is how the word is said, not spelt

explanation.surface: Someone spending hours in a stupor, or so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one long stupor; the definition is simply the plural, days being many hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by description: each of them holds 24 hours, so a plural of them is many hours.

clue.text: Remove garments from relative, including hot pants

indicators.note: pants as a verb, puffing and heaving, so the letters of HOT are shaken up

blocks.note: an uncle is a relative; it goes round OTH

explanation.surface: Taking off a relative's clothes, hot pants included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot pants' are very short shorts, so they look like the garments being removed; 'pants' is really the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the UN- prefix reverses clothing, just as undress reverses dress.
